Thanks — this is an intentional choice that matches the codebase-wide streaming convention. OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere, Anthropic and HuggingFace all log-and-continue on a single unparseable SSE event rather than aborting the whole stream, so a transient/malformed frame does not tank an otherwise-recoverable stream. ElevenLabs (the closest TTS analog) uses the same shape. I kept that behavior here for consistency.

That said, your underlying concern — a stream that yields *no* audio yet still emits a successful `done` — was valid, so I added a truncation guard after the read loop in `SpeechStream` (commit 0cbc820): if the stream ends without Cartesia's terminal `done` event **and** zero audio chunks were delivered, it now surfaces an error (`cartesia stream ended before any audio was received`, wrapping `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`) instead of a clean empty done. Partial-then-EOF is still treated as success, matching the other providers.

Good catch on the root concern. Treating a normal `io.EOF` as success (and emitting the final done) is the established convention here — ElevenLabs' `SpeechStream` breaks on EOF and emits its done the same way, and none of the SSE providers enforce a "saw terminal marker" invariant on EOF. So a *partial* stream that delivered audio before an early EOF stays a success, matching everything else.

For the specific case you flagged — a disconnect *before any audio and before* `done` — I added a guard in commit 0cbc820: `!sawDone && chunkIndex < 0` now produces an error rather than a successful empty done. That closes the "truncated to nothing, reported as success" hole without diverging from the provider-wide EOF handling for the partial-data case.

You're right, and I verified it against Cartesia's docs. The `/tts/sse` API documents the `done` event (done:true) as "the final event in the stream" for a successful generation, so a stream that reaches EOF without seeing `done` is truncated — regardless of how many chunks arrived first. My earlier guard (zero-chunks-only) was too narrow.

Fixed in commit 5c23c0a: the guard is now `!sawDone` (chunk count no longer matters). Any EOF before the terminal `done` event surfaces an error (`cartesia stream ended before the terminal done event (truncated audio)`, or the "before any audio" variant for the zero-chunk case) instead of emitting a successful `speech.audio.done` over partial audio. Success now depends on seeing Cartesia's `done` event, exactly as you suggested.

This intentionally diverges from the ElevenLabs EOF=success handling, because ElevenLabs is raw binary with no terminal marker whereas Cartesia has an explicit one. Verified `SpeechSynthesisStream` (5/5) and `SpeechSynthesisStreamAdvanced` (8/8) still pass, confirming the `done` event is present on normal completion.

This is the same concern as the sibling thread at line 338, where we already converged: a single mid-stream chunk that fails to base64-decode is logged and skipped, matching the log-and-continue convention that Gemini/OpenAI/Cohere/Anthropic use for individual chunk failures — an isolated bad frame becomes a brief audio glitch rather than a total stream failure. You acknowledged that as an accepted product tradeoff and marked it resolved.

Note that the truncation guard was also tightened in commit 5c23c0a: it now errors on any EOF that arrives before Cartesia's terminal `done` event, so a stream that is genuinely incomplete (truncated before `done`) is caught regardless of chunk decode outcomes. The only case that remains a silent skip is a decode failure on an individual chunk within an otherwise-complete stream that still delivers its `done` event.

This is intentional and is a deliberate alignment, not a new behavior introduced for streaming.

The non-streaming path already classifies *every* pre-first-byte `Do()` failure as a retriable upstream connection error - see `makeRequestWithDoFunc` in `core/providers/utils/utils.go:199`:

```go
// The HTTP request itself failed (e.g., connection error, fasthttp timeout).
return latency, NewBifrostUpstreamConnectionError(schemas.ErrProviderDoRequest, err), noop
```

This PR brings the streaming branches (`SpeechStream`, `PassthroughStream`) into line with that pre-existing classification, and the identical change was applied uniformly across all providers (openai, anthropic, cohere, gemini, huggingface, azure) in this stack. Narrowing only Azure's streaming branches would make Azure inconsistent with both its own non-streaming path and every other provider, while leaving the same idempotency tradeoff untouched everywhere else.

On the idempotency concern itself: replays only occur when the operator explicitly configures `max_retries > 0`; with the default no extra application-level retry happens. A provably-stale-vs-ambiguous distinction at the `Do()` boundary is a broader cross-cutting decision that would need to apply to the non-streaming path too, so it is better tracked as a separate change rather than diverging Azure streaming here.
